reading_method: Actual local scans, Tesseract OCR and agent visual review of source-linked crops. These are reviewed readings, not an independently labeled perception benchmark.

cases.name: South Fork Bridge (1928)
notes: Imperial dimensions take precedence over the conflicting printed 34.2M conversion.
Width and intrados rise are scaled from the plan/elevation; parapet decoration and internal fill are not resolved.

cases.name: Springfield–Des Arc Bridge (1871–1874)
notes: Upper arch is fitted to the elevation silhouette; sixteen panels are visible, but intermediate node stations are an equal-panel idealization.
3-inch timber decking is explicit. Built-up chords/eyebars are represented by envelopes unless individual section dimensions are confirmed.

cases.name: Wyman Bridge (1906)

evidence.quote: 170'-0" overall center to center of pins; 119'-0" approach

notes: The transverse clear width is not legible as a dimension; 4500mm is a declared visualization assumption.
Top-chord intermediate ordinates are visually estimated proportions; concrete deck thickness is unconfirmed.

cases.name: Old River Bridge (1891)
notes: Overall geometry follows the measured sheets, not the narrative's approximate 150-foot description.
Sagging/damaged deck shown in the scan is not reconstructed as surveyed deformation.

cases.name: Judsonia swing bridge (1923)
notes: The twelve-panel layout is idealized from the elevation; half-span dimension differs slightly from nominal 22-foot panel repetitions.
Approach truss heights are visually estimated at 0.5 and 0.8 times the main normal chord height; these are not dimension labels.
Swing span is saved closed. The swing_angle parameter provides schematic rigid-span rotation; gearing and joint mechanics are not reconstructed.

cases.name: Woolsey Creek Bridge (1947)
notes: Eight panels per span are visible. Equal-panel placement follows the overall span dimension; the approximate 18'-10" narrative panel length is not used as an exact chain.
Rolled I-beam and lattice details remain envelope-level representations.

cases.name: Fryer's Ford Bridge (1890–1891)
notes: The panel chain sums to 126'-2", 1/4 inch shorter than the overall dimension. Chain geometry is retained and this residual is reported rather than silently rescaled.

cases.name: Nimrod / Wallace Bridge (1908)
notes: Camelback ordinates between the dimensioned hip and crown are linearly interpolated along the visible top-chord segments.

cases.name: Ward's Crossing Bridge (1905)
notes: Hand-measured and laser-scan sheets are linked to one bridge, not counted as two bridges.
The laser-scan sheet's width differs from the measured sheet; it remains a cross-source check rather than a second geometry truth.

cases.name: DeGray Creek Bridge (circa 1915)
notes: Source explicitly states abutments were inaccessible and their form illustrative. Foundations are omitted rather than treated as surveyed geometry.

cases.name: Nineveh Falls / Hammonasset River bridge

evidence.quote: 230'-0" overall; 100'-0" clear span; 35'-2" cross section; 30'-0" roadway

notes: These TIFFs are engineering-drawing photographs of the Nineveh Falls concrete arch bridge, not a swing bridge.
Three rib lines and simplified spandrel supports are reconstructed. Rib widths and the deck/arch vertical separation remain explicit model assumptions.
Small arcade openings and bank profiles are simplified to posts and girders. The 5-foot main pier depth, approach post spacing and post sections are visualization assumptions, not surveyed details.

cases.name: Columbus Drive bascule bridge (UNSCALED REVIEW MODEL)

evidence.quote: Double leaf trunnion bascule; general arrangements

notes: 900-pixel source is too low resolution to confirm the main dimension chain. This model is normalized to 100000mm, NOT a real-world dimensioned reconstruction.

cases.name: Lake Shore Drive bascule bridge (UNSCALED REVIEW MODEL)

evidence.quote: Double leaf trunnion bascule; existing conditions and railing details

notes: General arrangement and rail-detail image belong to the same bridge. Absolute dimension chain remains unconfirmed at the supplied resolution; normalized visualization only.

cases.name: La Salle Street bascule bridge (UNSCALED REVIEW MODEL)

evidence.quote: Double leaf trunnion bascule bridge, La Salle Street

notes: Absolute dimensions cannot be established confidently from the 900-pixel drawing. The CAD is explicitly normalized and excluded from engineering-quantity accuracy claims.

cases.name: West Van Buren Street bascule bridge (UNSCALED REVIEW MODEL)

evidence.quote: Double leaf trunnion bascule, West Van Buren Street, South Branch Chicago River

notes: Unscaled review model. Bridge houses and navigation opening are schematic; no fabricated dimension labels are used as ground truth.
